EXPLANATION: Strong aliphatic C–H features (2880–2950 cm⁻¹ and 1454 cm⁻¹; cf. GFQ-003) indicate a simple alkyl system. The most intense band at 721 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of a ν(P=S) stretch in phosphorothioates, and the paired bands at 919/935 cm⁻¹ fit P–O(H) stretching modes. The weak 1206–1259 cm⁻¹ features do not show a dominant P=O band expected for phosphinic/oxide candidates, and there are no signatures for isocyanate (~2270 cm⁻¹), isothiocyanate (~2100 cm⁻¹), or C≡C (~2100 cm⁻¹), excluding other options. Thus CC P(O)(O)=S (phosphonothioic acid derivative) best matches the Raman pattern.
